title: The Biggest Launch Since ChatGPT
titleZh: ChatGPT 之后最大的一次发布
speaker: Alexandr Wang · Cleo Abram
desc: 68 分钟对谈：Meta 的 Alexandr Wang 讲 Muse 这个「个人 AI agent」到底能做什么、凭什么让人把隐私交给它、以及 AI 对齐与监管的真实分歧。口语密集、有抢话，适合练真实语流。

cues.en: What's happening right now is a big deal.
cues.zh: 现在正在发生的事，是件大事。

cues.en: This is the biggest launch since ChatGPT.
cues.zh: 这是自ChatGPT以来最重磅的一次发布。

cues.en: It's called Muse. "Muse." "Muse." "Has the tech world buzzing." "5 million downloads in 22 days." "Surpassing ChatGPT" And he built it.
cues.zh: 它叫Muse。“Muse。”“Muse。”“让科技圈炸开了锅。”“22天下载量500万。”“超越ChatGPT。”而它，是他做出来的。

cues.en: Most people are using AI to answer questions, basically glorified Google search.
cues.zh: 大多数人用AI就是问问题，说白了就是个高级点的谷歌搜索。

cues.en: This is something totally different.
cues.zh: 但这个完全不一样。

cues.en: "It's an AI agent" "Built for everyday life." "We believe that Muse will make you money." "One guy had Muse help plan a weekend away with his wife." It can make phone calls.
cues.zh: “它是一个AI智能体”“为日常生活而打造。”“我们相信Muse能帮你赚钱。”“有个人让Muse帮他策划和老婆的周末出游。”它能打电话。

cues.en: It can do tasks for you.
cues.zh: 它能替你办事。

cues.en: But for it to work, you have to trust it, first with your personal information, then to do what you actually want it to do, and then that it's not gonna, well, get out of control, all at a time when the most important AI leaders are warning
cues.zh: 但要让它发挥作用，你得信任它：先是要把个人信息交给它，然后要相信它会照你真正想要的那样去做，还要相信它不会——嗯，失控。而这一切，偏偏发生在最重要的那些AI领袖正在警告

cues.en: us that AI is getting out of control.
cues.zh: 我们说AI正在失控的时候。

cues.en: And I urge you to urge me to stop.
cues.zh: 我恳请你们，也来恳请我停下来。

cues.en: If you understand what's happening right now with Muse, you'll understand the biggest things happening in AI.
cues.zh: 如果你看懂了Muse现在发生的事，你也就看懂了AI领域当下最大的事。

cues.en: So what can it actually do?
cues.zh: 那它到底能做什么？

cues.en: When should we trust it?
cues.zh: 我们什么时候该信任它？

cues.en: And what do we need to do to make sure this goes right?
cues.zh: 我们又该做什么，才能确保这一切走在正轨上？

cues.en: And we're at the moment of, like, peak insanity.
cues.zh: 我们现在正处在一个疯狂到顶点的时刻。

cues.en: Why are all these billionaires obsessed with restaurant reservations?
cues.zh: 为什么这些亿万富翁都痴迷于餐厅订位？

cues.en: We have a shared interest in making sure this technology does not go horribly wrong.
cues.zh: 确保这项技术不出可怕的岔子，是我们共同的利益所在。

cues.en: Is that something that's happening in some private room somewhere?
cues.zh: 那是发生在某个密室里的事吗？

cues.en: The degree to which certain personal animosities are actually defining how they're developing this really important technology is insane to me.
cues.zh: 某些私人恩怨竟然在实实在在地左右他们如何开发这项至关重要的技术，这在我看来简直离谱。

cues.en: Amazing Let's do this.
cues.zh: 太棒了，开始吧。

cues.en: Okay. Welcome.
cues.zh: 好，欢迎。

cues.en: How have you been?
cues.zh: 你最近怎么样？

cues.en: I'm good.
cues.zh: 我挺好的。

cues.en: I'm really good.
cues.zh: 我非常好。

cues.en: How have you been?
cues.zh: 你最近怎么样？

cues.en: This is- It's been kind of insane, yeah.
cues.zh: 这真是——有点疯狂，是啊。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 是啊。

cues.en: What does it feel like?
cues.zh: 感觉怎么样？

cues.en: We didn't expect that it would be such a hit, so I feel amazing for, like, the whole team and everyone who, like, worked so hard on it 'cause it's, like, it's really come together and become a thing.
cues.zh: 我们没想到它会这么火，所以我觉得特别棒，为整个团队，也为所有为此拼命努力的人，因为这件事真的凑到了一起，成了一件了不起的事。

cues.en: So… That's what I'm excited to talk about.
cues.zh: 所以……这就是我很想聊的。

cues.en: I know you know all about the show already.
cues.zh: 我知道你对这个节目已经了如指掌了。

cues.en: But this isn't, like, a traditional interview.
cues.zh: 但这不是那种传统的采访。

cues.en: Like, I'm not gonna ask about financials.
cues.zh: 我不会问财务方面的事。

cues.en: I'm not gonna ask about management style.
cues.zh: 也不会问管理风格。

cues.en: You just launched one of the most popular consumer tools of all time, and so the only thing that I wanna know is what's the future that you're working toward
cues.zh: 你刚刚发布了史上最受欢迎的消费级工具之一，所以我唯一想知道的是，你在朝着什么样的未来努力——

cues.en: with that tool, and how can this audience that's really optimistic and really wants to be part of making sure that that future go right, how can they feel like they're part of the decisions that are being made?
cues.zh: 用这个工具，还有这些观众，他们特别乐观，也特别想参与进来，确保那个未来能走对方向，他们怎么才能觉得自己也参与了这些正在做的决定？

cues.en: Yep.
cues.zh: 对。

cues.en: All of that.
cues.zh: 就这些。

cues.en: Yeah. That's what we do.
cues.zh: 对，这就是我们做的事。

cues.en: One of the reasons I wanted to talk to you was I've always appreciated that you're really blunt.
cues.zh: 我想跟你聊的一个原因，是我一直很欣赏你说话特别直。

cues.en: Like, I, I honestly think that people need straight talk about this.
cues.zh: 说实话，我真的觉得大家需要有人把话说清楚。

cues.en: I think that they feel confused, and I wanna get at what's really happening, what have you built, how are people using it, how are they not, what are the real challenges.
cues.zh: 我觉得大家很困惑，我想弄清楚到底发生了什么，你们做出了什么，人们在怎么用它，又为什么不用，真正的挑战是什么。

cues.en: I think one other interesting thing is given how popular Muse has become, I want to use it as a way to talk about other things in AI.
cues.zh: 还有一点挺有意思的：考虑到 Muse 已经这么火，我想借它来聊聊 AI 的其他方面。

cues.en: Awesome.
cues.zh: 太好了。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: Let's get into it.
cues.zh: 那我们开始吧。

cues.en: Muse is the fastest-growing consumer tool since ChatGPT.
cues.zh: Muse 是 ChatGPT 之后增长最快的消费级工具。

cues.en: Faster than ChatGPT, I think, and it feels like this is the moment when we're moving maybe from chatbots to agents, but there have been a lot of other popular agents, mostly in code, and I'm curious, why do you think
cues.zh: 我觉得比 ChatGPT 还快，而且感觉现在正是我们从聊天机器人走向智能体的时刻，不过也有很多别的智能体很火，主要是在编程领域，我很好奇，你觉得为什么

cues.en: this is happening for Muse right now?
cues.zh: 为什么现在这事发生在 Muse 身上？

cues.en: Why is Muse exploding like this?
cues.zh: 为什么 Muse 会这样爆发式增长？

cues.en: I think one of the mysteries of AI so far this year, for most of the year, has been that agents were happening for engineers and software engineers and coders, and then nobody else in the world, like, was experiencing it, knew what it was, like,
cues.zh: 我觉得今年到目前为止，AI最让人费解的一点是，大部分时间里，智能体只存在于工程师、软件工程师和程序员的世界里，而世界上其他人根本没体验过，也不知道它是什么，

cues.en: understood exactly what was happening.
cues.zh: 不明白到底在发生什么。

cues.en: And so for most of this year, you've kind of had this, like, two dialogues almost where people who do code and could see how powerful AI was becoming
cues.zh: 所以今年大部分时间，几乎存在两种对话，会写代码、能看到AI变得多强大的人

cues.en: and, and how useful it was becoming were like, "Oh my gosh, this is incredible."
cues.zh: 以及它变得多有用的人会说：“天哪，这太不可思议了。”

cues.en: And then everyone else was kind of like, "What are you talking about?
cues.zh: 而其他人则是：“你们在说什么？

cues.en: I just still use a chatbot.
cues.zh: 我还是只用聊天机器人。

cues.en: Like, it's, like, a little bit better than Google, but what are you guys all freaked out about?" And, um, and one of the things that we were really excited to do is how do we take the magic that engineers and coders and developers
cues.zh: 它也就比谷歌好一点，你们到底在激动什么？”我们特别想做的一件事，就是把工程师、程序员和开发者

cues.en: are seeing and bring that to everyone?
cues.zh: 所看到的魔力带给所有人。

cues.en: One of the things that, that has happened over the course of the past year is, like, the AI models started out as pretty janky agents, and you kind of had to struggle through them to get them to work, and then they slowly got better and better and better.
cues.zh: 过去一年发生的一件事是，AI模型一开始作为智能体还挺粗糙的，你得费劲折腾才能让它工作，然后它们慢慢变得越来越好。

cues.en: And most of the industry's been really focused on making them just, like- Better and better and better at coding.
cues.zh: 而且行业里大多数人一直专注于让它们在编程方面越来越好。

cues.en: But we really felt this was like a s- a big gap because most people in the world, they don't know how to code.
cues.zh: 但我们真切感受到这是一个巨大的鸿沟，因为世界上大多数人不会编程。

cues.en: They d- probably never even want to code.
cues.zh: 他们可能根本不想编程。

cues.en: Um, but they still wanna feel the experience of agents and, um, having AI that is able to do more for you and actually start taking on more end-to-end workflows and take on more tasks for you.
cues.zh: 但他们仍然想体验智能体，想拥有能为你做更多事的AI，真正开始承担更多端到端的工作流程，为你完成更多任务。

cues.en: So that was really the goal behind Muse, and I think we spent a lot of time polishing all the little details to make sure that it would just work for people
cues.zh: 这就是Muse背后的目标，我们花了很多时间打磨所有细节，确保它能直接为人们所用

cues.en: because we knew that, like, developers can kind of withstand a lot of jank and a lot of stuff breaking and, like, they can kind of deal with all of that because, you know, they're, they're…
cues.zh: 因为我们知道，开发者能忍受很多粗糙和出问题的地方，他们能应付这些，因为，你知道，他们……

cues.en: It's technology.
cues.zh: 这是技术。

cues.en: They're used to dealing with, you know- Yeah … unripe technology.
cues.zh: 他们习惯了应对，你知道——对……不成熟的技术。

cues.en: But for everyone, you have to make something that's really smooth and, and really works for them.
cues.zh: 但对大众来说，你必须做出真正顺畅、真正好用的东西。

cues.en: That also helps explain the big gap, I think, between what it feels like for most people to actually use AI, when they were using a chatbot in particular, and the
cues.zh: 我觉得这也解释了为什么大多数人实际使用AI的感受，尤其是用聊天机器人时，和

cues.en: conversation around AI that's it's gonna take everyone's jobs, it's really scary.
cues.zh: 围绕AI的讨论——说它会抢走所有人的工作、非常可怕——之间存在巨大差距。

cues.en: It's, you know, there's a, there's a macro conversation happening, and then there's an experience that people are having.
cues.zh: 你知道，一边是宏观层面的讨论，另一边是人们真实的体验。

cues.en: And it just seems like those things are really, really far apart.
cues.zh: 而这两者似乎相距非常非常远。

cues.en: And to your point, Muse is giving more people the opportunity to have the insight that computer engineers had, you know, call it a year ago.
cues.zh: 就像你说的，Muse让更多人有机会获得计算机工程师一年前就有的那种洞察。

cues.en: Yeah. Is that fair?
cues.zh: 对，这么说合理吗？

cues.en: I, I think that's true, yeah.
cues.zh: 我，我觉得是这样，没错。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 是啊。

cues.en: There are also moments in history that I think feel similar.
cues.zh: 我觉得历史上也有一些时刻和现在很像。

cues.en: Would you say it's like the mobile phone moment for agents?
cues.zh: 你会说这就像智能体的“手机时刻”吗？

cues.en: There are, you know, billions of people brought online by mobile phones that never had PCs because it was easy and simple to use, and they didn't, you know. I actually hadn't thought about that until you just mentioned it, but I think it's a great analogy because it's
cues.zh: 手机让数十亿从没用过电脑的人上了网，因为它简单易用，而他们以前没有……你刚才提到之前，我其实没想过这一点，但我觉得这是个很好的类比，因为……

cues.en: These models, they're improving really fast, and they're improving really, really quickly.
cues.zh: 这些模型进步得非常快，真的非常快。

cues.en: And it's really important that we, as those models get better, that the, the superpowers that they, they lend can be given to, like, literally everyone all around the world.
cues.zh: 很重要的一点是，随着这些模型变得更强，它们带来的那些“超能力”能真正给到世界各地的每一个人。

cues.en: The part that I like about the analogy is, like, um, so much of it is just about figuring out how to package it all together into a form factor that, um, will resonate with people, and that's what we spent a lot of time trying to
cues.zh: 我喜欢这个类比的地方在于，很多工作其实就是要把它整合成一种能让人产生共鸣的产品形态，而这就是我们花了很多时间想要去……

cues.en: craft and get right and, and make perfect.
cues.zh: 打磨、做对，并做到完美。

cues.en: Which also gets to one of the interesting initial reactions that I've heard of Muse, which is, is everybody's life more complicated than mine?
cues.zh: 这也引出了我听到过的关于 Muse 的一个很有意思的初期反应：难道每个人的生活都比我的更复杂吗？

cues.en: Like, I wake up, I go to work, I play with my kids, I have one restaurant reservation a month, I plan one vacation with my spouse.
cues.zh: 比如我起床、上班、陪孩子玩，一个月订一次餐厅，和伴侣计划一次度假。

cues.en: Like, why are all these billionaires obsessed with restaurant reservations?
cues.zh: 为什么这些亿万富翁都这么执着于订餐厅？

cues.en: Why do I need an assistant?
cues.zh: 我为什么需要一个助手？

cues.en: How would you answer that?
cues.zh: 你会怎么回答？

cues.en: Whenever I explain Muse to someone just who knows nothing about it, um, I just say, like, Muse can help save you money and save you time, and everybody in the world wants to save money and wants to save time.
cues.zh: 每当我向完全不了解 Muse 的人解释它时，我就说，Muse 能帮你省钱、省时间，而世界上每个人都想省钱、省时间。

cues.en: Depending on what your lifestyle is, that can mean a different thing to you.
cues.zh: 取决于你的生活方式，这对你来说可能意味着不同的事情。

cues.en: I think almost everyone has, like, subscriptions that they shouldn't be paying for or subscriptions that are really expensive, like cable bills or insurance, and for a lot of people, their magic moment with Muse is just saving
cues.zh: 我觉得几乎每个人都有一些不该付的订阅，或者特别贵的订阅，比如有线电视费或保险；对很多人来说，Muse 让他们惊艳的时刻就是省下……

cues.en: money on things that they shouldn't be spending money on or they shouldn't be spending so much money on, or finding gift cards that they hadn't spent or, you know, the list goes on and on and on.
cues.zh: 那些不该花的钱，或者不该花那么多钱的东西上的钱，或者找到还没用掉的礼品卡，这样的例子还有很多很多。

cues.en: I think it's awesome that so many people are experiencing that.
cues.zh: 我觉得这么多人能有这种体验，真的很棒。

cues.en: I think that's, like, great because these are things that, they're just, I think for most people, they're just so boring- That you would never get to Yeah, actually, like, handling them or, or dealing with them, but, you know, your agent, Muse, can just do that for you.
cues.zh: 我觉得这很好，因为对大多数人来说，这些事太无聊了，你根本不会去处理它们；但你的智能体 Muse 可以直接替你做。

cues.en: And then they're saving time, which I think for, for lots of people, I think there are always experiences that are just way more frustrating than they should be, like going to the DMV is one example.
cues.zh: 然后他们还能省时间。我觉得对很多人来说，总有一些体验本不该那么让人抓狂，比如去车管所就是一个例子。

cues.en: We actually, when we built Muse, we, like, specifically tested it to see if it could deal with the DMV website because that was, like, the pinnacle we thought
cues.zh: 其实我们在做 Muse 的时候，专门测试过它能不能处理车管所网站，因为在我们看来，那就是……

cues.en: of, like, the most frustrating experience for any human is dealing with the DMV.
cues.zh: 人类最抓狂体验的顶峰：和车管所打交道。

cues.en: So we kne- we needed to have Muse, like, be able to, to do well in that situation.
cues.zh: 所以我们需要让 Muse 能在那种情况下也表现出色。

cues.en: We've seen people use it for, like, yeah, navigating the healthcare system's a big one.
cues.zh: 我们见过有人用它来处理医疗系统，这一块需求很大。

cues.en: Medical claims is, like, a huge one that, like, most people just… It's, like, so complicated and annoying that it's just, like, incredibly frustrating.
cues.zh: 医疗理赔就是一个很大的用例，大多数人……它又复杂又烦人，真的让人特别抓狂。

cues.en: We've seen people, like, use it to help run their small business.
cues.zh: 我们见过有人用它来帮忙经营小生意。

cues.en: We've seen a lot of people, like, use it to help run their social media even, and I think the medical system is a really good example 'cause it's, like, so hard to understand.
cues.zh: 我们见过很多人甚至用它来帮忙运营社交媒体，而且我觉得医疗系统就是个很好的例子，因为它真的很难搞懂。

cues.en: And I think the, the you know, one of the best ways to put it is, like, I think the cases where people…
cues.zh: 我觉得，最好的说法之一是，我认为在那些人们……的情况下

cues.en: where it's, like, a huge lifesaver are the cases where, like, otherwise you would be at your computer, you'd have to Google, like, 50 different things.
cues.zh: 它能帮上大忙的情况，就是本来你得坐在电脑前，得去搜大概五十种不同的东西。

cues.en: You have to read, go to, like, 100 different websites and try to figure out what the hell is going on, and it could, it's just, like, this incredibly frustrating experience, or you could have your Muse do it.
cues.zh: 你得读资料、上大概一百个不同的网站，试图搞明白到底怎么回事，那简直是一种让人无比崩溃的体验；或者，你可以让你的 Muse 来做。

cues.en: I also think about how many things I suspect are made difficult and time-consuming on purpose in order to frustrate me so much that I don't get to the end?
cues.zh: 我也会想，有多少事情我怀疑是故意被弄得又难又耗时，就是为了把我烦到放弃，不让我走到最后？

cues.en: How many claims are actually designed to be that hard so that I give up?
cues.zh: 有多少索赔申请其实被设计得那么难，就是为了让我放弃？

cues.en: And I wonder what effect more people having more patience because they have support will have on that kind of systems engineering.
cues.zh: 我也想知道，更多人因为有了支持而变得更有耐心，会对那种系统设计产生什么影响。

cues.en: One of the, the little memes that I made of the little Muse was, uh, Muse in Hood, which is like a Muse Robin Hood.
cues.zh: 我给小 Muse 做的一个小梗图是，呃，Muse in Hood，就像 Muse 版的罗宾汉。

cues.en: But I think there's, like, a real truth to this, which is there are lots of things that exist in the world that are, to your point, meant to be hard so that mo-
cues.zh: 但我觉得这里面确实有点道理：世界上有很多东西，就像你说的，本来就是故意设计得很难，好让更……

cues.en: like, uh, canceling subscriptions is one of the best examples, where there's some subscriptions where you have to, like, click on one thing and click on another thing, and then click on, like, the little piece of text, and then not click the big
cues.zh: 比如，呃，取消订阅就是最好的例子之一：有些订阅你得点这个、再点那个，然后点那一小段文字，还不能点那个大……

cues.en: red button, but click the other button.
cues.zh: 红色按钮，而要点击另一个按钮。

cues.en: And, like, that's just, like, the perfect example where there's lots of cases where things are designed to be hard for people, and I think, like, this is giving people the tools to be able to just do those things seamlessly and easily.
cues.zh: 这就是个完美的例子，说明有很多情况都是故意把东西设计得让人很难操作；我觉得这正是在给人们工具，让他们能顺畅轻松地完成这些事。

cues.en: I got access to the calling, um, and I had it make a call this morning, which it did successfully.
cues.zh: 我获得了打电话功能的权限，呃，今天早上我让它打了个电话，它成功打出去了。

cues.en: What does it sound like on the other end?
cues.zh: 电话那头听起来怎么样？

cues.en: I think it's clear for the other end that it is, like, an AI, and I think if you look, read the, you know, we show, we show users the transcript.
cues.zh: 我觉得电话那头能明显听出来它是 AI；而且如果你看、读一下，你知道，我们会给用户看通话记录。

cues.en: Like, if you see the transcript, like, the beginning of the call I always think is really funny because it's like, "Hi, I'm so-and-so.
cues.zh: 比如，如果你看通话记录，通话开头我总觉得特别好笑，因为它是这样的：“嗨，我是某某。”

cues.en: Um, I'm Cleo's assistant, and, uh, this call is being recorded." And I think it's just, like, always this very funny beginning of a call. "Hi, I'm Haley calling on Cleo Abrams' behalf.
cues.zh: “呃，我是 Cleo 的助理，呃，这通电话正在录音。”我觉得这开头总是特别好笑。“嗨，我是 Haley，代表 Cleo Abrams 打来电话。”

cues.en: I'm transcribing our call for notes." What are some examples of when it's messed up for you or when it's, you feel like categories it struggles for still?
cues.zh: “我会为记录把我们的通话转成文字。”有没有一些例子，是它搞砸的时候，或者你觉得它仍然不擅长的类别？

cues.en: One thing that we're, we're always trying to improve is the memory of these Of these agents, right?
cues.zh: 我们一直在努力改进的一点，就是这些智能体的记忆，对吧？

cues.en: And this is still one of the more unsolved problems, I think, for a lot of these agents, is having the— You know, the, the memory of the agents is, like, not like that of a human.
cues.zh: 我觉得对很多这类智能体来说，这仍然是比较未解决的问题之一，就是拥有——你知道，智能体的记忆并不像人类那样。

cues.en: Um, sometimes it can feel like it's like that, but it is really different.
cues.zh: 呃，有时候感觉好像差不多，但其实真的很不一样。

cues.en: So that's one area where we're, like, always trying to improve.
cues.zh: 所以这是我们一直在努力改进的一个方面。

cues.en: We always wanna, wanna figure out how to make the agents better.
cues.zh: 我们总是想、想弄清楚怎么让这些智能体变得更好。

cues.en: And then, like, we want them to be able to continue doing more and more complex tasks.
cues.zh: 然后，我们希望它们能够继续完成越来越复杂的任务。

cues.en: I, I find this really funny, but there's, um, there's a lot of people who will just, like, ask their Muse, "I want you to make me $10,000."
cues.zh: 我觉得这挺有意思的，但有很多人会直接跟自己的 Muse 说：“我想让你帮我赚一万美元。”

cues.en: And obviously, not everyone can just ask their Muse to make them $10,000, but, like, I think, I think these kinds of, like, more amorphous, nebulous tasks, like, we want Muse to be able to at least, like, build a plan and figure
cues.zh: 显然，不是所有人都能直接让 Muse 帮自己赚一万美元，但我觉得像这种比较模糊、不太明确的任务，我们希望 Muse 至少能制定计划并搞清楚

cues.en: out and, you know, you're gonna have to do your part if you wanna make $10,000.
cues.zh: 接下来该怎么做；而且你要知道，想赚到一万美元，你自己也得出力。

cues.en: But I think we wanna enable the, the agent to do more and more kind of complex and esoteric tasks, um, to help the users.
cues.zh: 但我觉得我们希望让这个智能体完成越来越多复杂又冷门的任务，来帮助用户。

cues.en: There are some things where I feel emotionally, even if Muse could do them, I would prefer that they didn't.
cues.zh: 有些事情，从情感上我觉得，就算 Muse 能做，我也希望它别做。

cues.en: So for example, if I'm texting a friend and I find out that their Muse agent is responding to me, I would be offended by that.
cues.zh: 比如，如果我在给朋友发消息，结果发现是朋友的 Muse 智能体在回复我，我会觉得被冒犯了。

cues.en: Are there categories of things that you think explicitly Muse should not do that are sort- just, like, extremely deprioritized, not because they're technically that hard, but because socially, not the point?
cues.zh: 有没有哪类事情，你觉得 Muse 明确不该做，应该被排到极低优先级？不是因为技术上有多难，而是从社交角度说，根本没必要？

cues.en: A lot of what we care about is, like having Muse kind of like clear the way such that you can spend more time on the things that you want to do and the things that you enjoy doing, and the things that are, like, valuable to you.
cues.zh: 我们很在意的一点，是让 Muse 帮你扫清障碍，这样你就能把更多时间花在想做的事、喜欢做的事，以及对你有价值的事上。

cues.en: We generally speaking want to figure out how to make someone's Muse is like a different entity than them.
cues.zh: 总的来说，我们想弄清楚怎样让一个人的 Muse 成为和他本人不同的实体。

cues.en: That's why it's like a little cute guy.
cues.zh: 所以它才被设计成一个可爱的小家伙。

cues.en: Um, uh, and, and we want to, over time, continue making that more and more clear because, um, to your point, like it is socially weird if you're like you think you're talking to your friend and it just happens to be the
cues.zh: 而且我们希望随着时间推移，这一点能越来越清楚，因为就像你说的，如果你以为自己是在跟朋友聊天，结果却是那个

cues.en: little Muse, the little Muse guy- Yeah behind the, behind the curtain.
cues.zh: 小 Muse，那个小 Muse 小家伙——对，在幕后。

cues.en: Speaking of what they look like, one of the things I've visited humanoid robots before, and one of the things they spend a lot of time thinking about is how to make it cute so that you like them and you want them in your home, or at least you're not afraid of them.
cues.zh: 说到它们长什么样，我以前参观过人形机器人，它们花很多时间思考的一件事，就是怎么把它做得可爱，让你喜欢它、想把它带回家，或者至少不怕它。

cues.en: What did Muse look like in previous iterations, and how did you decide on that particular guy?
cues.zh: Muse 在之前的版本里长什么样，你们又是怎么决定用现在这个形象的？

cues.en: I think this is, like, one of the most shocking things.
cues.zh: 我觉得这算是最让人意外的点之一。

cues.en: What the Muse looks like now is what he looked like in the very first prototype.
cues.zh: Muse 现在的样子，就是它最初原型的样子。

cues.en: It's kind of one of these, like, rare things where the, the very first version was just perfect and then just, like, grew on all of us, and we ended up going with it.
cues.zh: 这算是很少见的情况：第一版就刚刚好，后来越看越顺眼，最后我们就用了它。

cues.en: We had lots of debates about it, uh, which are, you know, in retrospect will be some of my funniest meetings of like, you know, a bunch of serious adults
cues.zh: 我们为此争论过很多次，回想起来，这会是我开过的最搞笑的会之一：一群严肃的成年人

cues.en: getting in a room, like arguing about this cute little, um, you know, character.
cues.zh: 聚在一个房间里，为这个可爱的小角色争来争去。

cues.en: But, uh, but yeah, I mean, I think we were like, is it not serious enough?
cues.zh: 不过是啊，我的意思是，我们当时会想：它是不是不够严肃？

cues.en: Is it, like, too playful?
cues.zh: 是不是太爱玩了？

cues.en: Does he need to be more colorful?
cues.zh: 它需要更鲜艳一点吗？

cues.en: Like, these were, like, all things that we asked the questions on, and we looked at them.
cues.zh: 这些都是我们问过、也考虑过的问题。

cues.en: We're like, "No, he's perfect." What is the big vision here?
cues.zh: 我们说：“不，它很完美。”那这里的大愿景是什么？

cues.en: I sometimes struggle when talking to AI leaders to push people to think about more than, like, five years out.
cues.zh: 有时候我跟 AI 领导者交流时，会很难推动他们去思考五年以后的事情。

cues.en: But what is, what is the vision here?
cues.zh: 但这儿的愿景到底是什么？

cues.en: Is it that Muse becomes my layer on everything on the internet?
cues.zh: 是让 Muse 成为我在互联网上处理一切事情的那一层吗？

cues.en: Is it, like, map this out for me if it goes the way that you hope it does.
cues.zh: 如果事情按你希望的方向发展，给我描绘一下会是什么样。

cues.en: What we really want Muse to be over time is kind of this, like, general manager, so to speak, that helps you accomplish all the things you want out of life.
cues.zh: 随着时间推移，我们真正希望 Muse 成为的，可以说是一个总管，帮你实现人生中想要完成的所有事情。

cues.en: So, like, I think, I think one of the kind of tragedies of the modern world is
cues.zh: 我觉得现代世界的一个可悲之处在于

cues.en: that, like, um, most people have wants and dreams, um, that can range from, like, really big ideas, like, hey, I want to start a company, or I want to cure
cues.zh: 大多数人都有愿望和梦想，范围从特别宏大的想法，比如“我想创办一家公司”，或者“我想治愈

cues.en: disease, or I wanna save the planet, all the way to, you know, small wants that are like, hey, I wanna spend more time with my family and, uh, I want to eat healthier.
cues.zh: 疾病”，或者“我想拯救地球”，一直到那些很小的愿望，比如“我想多陪陪家人”，还有“我想吃得更健康”。

cues.en: And, you know, um, and, and there's a whole range, but for most people, I think there's just so many- barriers and burdens in the way.
cues.zh: 这些愿望有大有小，但对大多数人来说，我觉得路上有太多障碍和负担。

cues.en: What I really hope it accomplishes is help every single one of the eight billion people all around the world be able to, uh, accomplish their wants and dreams.
cues.zh: 我真正希望它能做到的是，帮助全世界八十亿人中的每一个人实现自己的愿望和梦想。

cues.en: And, um, I think this is like, you know, if we are able to accomplish that, like, I think the world will seem insane.
cues.zh: 我觉得，如果我们真能做到这一点，世界会变得不可思议。

cues.en: That's what we really want Muse to be and what, what we think it can, it can be, uh, if we keep working at it.
cues.zh: 这就是我们真正希望 Muse 成为的样子，也是我们相信只要持续努力它就能成为的样子。

cues.en: You know, it's really nice to hear you talk about giving people time back because for a really long time I have felt, and I think a lot of people have feel, have felt like So much of the financial incentive of most tech products
cues.zh: 听你谈到把时间还给人们，真的很不错，因为很长一段时间以来我都觉得，而且我觉得很多人也有同感：大多数科技产品很大一部分的经济激励，

cues.en: that I use, especially the ones that are ad backed, is to take my time, is to distract me from the things that I want.
cues.zh: 尤其是我用的那些靠广告支撑的产品，就是占用我的时间，让我从自己真正想做的事情上分心。

cues.en: Muse is free right now.
cues.zh: Muse 目前是免费的。

cues.en: It probably will have ads in the future.
cues.zh: 未来它很可能会加广告。

cues.en: Is there a tension between giving people their time back and having an ads-based business, or are there other incentives about, like, Muse steering
cues.zh: 把时间还给用户和做广告生意之间是否存在矛盾？还是说还有其他动机，比如让 Muse 引导

cues.en: me down a path that isn't quite what I said I wanted because it's ad backed?
cues.zh: 我走上一条并不完全是我说自己想要的路，因为它是靠广告盈利的？

cues.en: How do you add ads to a product like this?
cues.zh: 你们会怎么在这样一个产品里加广告？

cues.en: First off, like, I think right now it's, it's free.
cues.zh: 首先，我觉得现在它是免费的。

cues.en: There are subscription tiers.
cues.zh: 我们有订阅套餐。

cues.en: I think we think that there's plenty of, of, um, business models that are really aligned with user around, like, for example, if they, um, if they're buying things using Muse or Muse is saving them money or, um, Muse
cues.zh: 我觉得我们认为有很多真正与用户利益一致的商业模式，比如，如果用户用 Muse 购物，或者 Muse 帮他们省钱，或者 Muse

cues.en: is making them money, like figuring out a way to, to take some small fee on, on those kinds of transactions.
cues.zh: 帮他们赚钱，那我们就可以想办法在这类交易中收取一点小额费用。

cues.en: Um, so I wouldn't say we're spending that much time thinking about, um, you know, ads necessarily right now.
cues.zh: 所以我不会说我们现在花了很多时间专门考虑广告。

cues.en: That being said, like, I don't think ad-based models are necessarily synonymous with, like, you needing to take all of your time.
cues.zh: 话虽如此，我不认为靠广告的模式就一定意味着要占用你的全部时间。

cues.en: I think Google Ads are a really good example of this, where, yeah.
cues.zh: 我觉得谷歌广告就是一个很好的例子，嗯，对。

cues.en: when I go to Google, my, my dream is to get in and get out, and I don't think Google's really trying to stop me from getting in and getting out.
cues.zh: 我用谷歌的时候，我的梦想就是进去、出来，赶紧完事，我不觉得谷歌真的想拦着我进去再出来。

cues.en: But they've built something obviously pretty incredible, and so, yeah, I don't think it's a necessity by any means.
cues.zh: 但他们确实做出了相当了不起的东西，所以，是啊，我绝不认为这是必需的。

cues.en: Um, I think, again, I think if we actually accomplish this thing that I'm saying, which is people are using Muse to, uh, really, like, do the things that they want to do and do…
cues.zh: 嗯，我觉得，再说一次，我觉得如果我们真的做成了我说的这件事，也就是人们用 Muse 真正去做他们想做的事，并且去……

cues.en: and, like, really, like, you know, in a non-corny way, like, accomplish their dreams, I think it's, I, you know, I think there's gonna be a lot of ways to, to make that sustainable.
cues.zh: 而且，真正地，不是那种肉麻的方式，去实现他们的梦想，我觉得，你知道，我觉得会有很多办法让这件事持续下去。

cues.en: So when I think about mapping out a future to get there, to this optimistic vision, one of the most important things is what do we need to get right, what challenges do we need to avoid in order to make that true?
cues.zh: 所以当我思考如何规划未来、走向那个乐观愿景时，最重要的事情之一是：我们需要把什么做对，需要避开哪些挑战，才能让它成真？

cues.en: I want to hear you use Muse and how you've dealt with these challenges at Muse as an example of larger questions in AI.
cues.zh: 我想听你谈谈你使用 Muse 的体验，以及 Muse 是如何应对这些挑战的，并把它当作 AI 更大议题的一个例子。

cues.en: I think everything that I'm about to say applies to basically every AI product, and I would be curious if you disagree with that.
cues.zh: 我觉得我接下来要说的，基本上适用于所有 AI 产品；如果你不同意，我倒是很好奇。

cues.en: I think there are basically three levels here.
cues.zh: 我觉得这里基本上有三个层面。

cues.en: Level one is privacy.
cues.zh: 第一个层面是隐私。

cues.en: So you say, "I download Muse." And then I get to the point where it asks to be connected to my Gmail, and I say, "Whoa, whoa, whoa, I'm not sure that I wanna do that.
cues.zh: 所以你说“我下载了 Muse”，然后到了它要连接我的 Gmail 那一步，我说：“等等等等，我不确定我想这么干。”

cues.en: Like nope, nope, I'm out." That, at the lowest level, is a concern about the relationship between the user and Muse itself, and therefore Meta.
cues.zh: 比如“不了不了，我退出”。在最基本的层面上，这是对用户和 Muse 本身、因而也是和 Meta 之间关系的担忧。

cues.en: So what is Meta going to do with my information?
cues.zh: 那么 Meta 会拿我的信息做什么？

cues.en: Could hackers get that information?
cues.zh: 黑客能拿到那些信息吗？

cues.en: And in some countries, can governments get that information somehow?
cues.zh: 而在一些国家，政府能不能以某种方式拿到那些信息？

cues.en: I know that you've spent a lot of time thinking about this.
cues.zh: 我知道你花了很多时间思考这个问题。

cues.en: I'd like to get as detailed as we possibly can here for a lay audience.
cues.zh: 我想尽量讲得详细一些，让普通听众也能听懂。

cues.en: What is the sentinel agent?
cues.zh: 什么是哨兵代理？

cues.en: What is Muse Confidential and Secure VM?
cues.zh: 什么是 Muse 的机密安全虚拟机？

cues.en: How do you think about this in terms of what can Muse see and not see, and things people should know about this first level of privacy?
cues.zh: 从 Muse 能看到什么、不能看到什么，以及人们应该了解的第一层隐私问题来看，你是怎么考虑这件事的？

cues.en: Muse is built on top of the, the secure VM, the Muse secure VM.
cues.zh: Muse 是构建在安全虚拟机之上的，也就是 Muse 安全虚拟机。

cues.en: And, um, that is a completely sandboxed virtual machine, uh, or think about it as like a, a mini sandbox computer- Mm-hmm that is sort of isolated.
cues.zh: 而且，那是一个完全沙箱化的虚拟机，或者你可以把它想成一台小小的沙箱电脑——它是相对隔离的。

cues.en: The information that you share with, with Muse is stored in that little secure computer.
cues.zh: 你和 Muse 分享的信息会存储在那台小小的安全电脑里。

cues.en: It is not stored elsewhere.
cues.zh: 它不会存储在别的地方。

cues.en: Um, and that little secure computer is sort of like your home, your Muse's home, so to speak.
cues.zh: 而且，那台小小的安全电脑可以说就像是你的家，也就是 Muse 的家。

cues.en: Inside that secure VM, you have a, uh… we have a very, uh, pretty sophisticated security architecture because, you know, we knew that privacy and security,
cues.zh: 在那个安全虚拟机里，有一个，呃……我们有一套非常，呃，相当精密的安全架构，因为，你知道，我们知道隐私和安全……

cues.en: frankly speaking, were gonna be some of the most important things for, for most consumers to, to get them to adopt it.
cues.zh: 坦白说，对大多数消费者来说，这将是促使他们采用它的最重要因素之一。

cues.en: So as you mentioned, we built a sentinel, a, uh, this sort of architecture with a sentinel agent.
cues.zh: 正如你提到的，我们构建了一个哨兵，也就是一种带有哨兵代理的架构。

cues.en: So the way it works is that, uh, the, the model or the AI agent on the inside, as it's, um, going about and, and doing its work, whenever it wants to, uh- communicate outwards.
cues.zh: 它的运作方式是，里面的模型或AI代理在开展工作、对外通信时，每当它想向外发送信息。

cues.en: So it, it wants to take any information and send it out, either to do, you know, um, fill it out on a website, or send a message, or make a phone call, or, you know, any case where it would take information from outside of that virtual
cues.zh: 它想拿取任何信息并发送出去，比如在网站上填写内容、发消息、打电话，或者任何要把信息带出那台虚拟

cues.en: machine, there's a separate agent, uh, the sentinel, that's watching and making sure that, um, it's kind of like a, almost like a traffic cop or something.
cues.zh: 机的场景；这时会有一个单独的代理——哨兵——在监控，并确保……它有点像交通警察之类的角色。

cues.en: It's just, like, making sure that, you know, uh, there's nothing, uh… It's not saying like, "Oh, whoa, whoa, whoa, that information, like, that's your credit card number or Social Security number," or whatever it might be.
cues.zh: 它只是在确保没什么问题……它不会说：“哦，等等等等，那个信息是你的信用卡号或社保号”之类的。

cues.en: Like, do not share that.
cues.zh: 比如“别分享那个”。

cues.en: That should stay, that should stay inside.
cues.zh: 那应该留在里面。

cues.en: And then the last thing that we do is, um, uh, a lot of human loop verifications.
cues.zh: 最后，我们还会做大量需要人工确认的验证。

cues.en: So whenever Muse wants to connect to a new website or send information to a new website, um, there will be, like, a little dialogue that pops up.
cues.zh: 所以每当Muse想连接新网站或向新网站发送信息时，都会弹出一个小对话框。

cues.en: Which asks the user, like, "Hey, are you okay with Muse contacting this website or sending information to this, this website," and whatnot.
cues.zh: 询问用户：“嘿，你介意Muse联系这个网站或向这个网站发送信息吗？”之类的。

cues.zh: 有些人说我们这样很烦，总是让人批准Muse把信息发到哪里。
